data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's separating property conflates two distinct concepts ('number-conserving or linear') and then uses the nonstructural property 'computationally universal' to predict rule 110 and rule 54 fail. Turing completeness is not a structural local-rule property and does not entail long transients on small finite rings; rule 110's universality is an asymptotic infinite-lattice fact, so it cannot separate the enumerated (rule,W) pairs as required. The rule 54 prediction rests on 'supports interacting glider structures similar to Rule 110', which is renamed data/asymptotic analogy rather than a checkable structural property, and it explicitly admits the prediction may fail on small widths. It also provides no runnable solve(rule, width) entry point and no filed per-(rule,width) simulation tables, only a verbal description of how one would check.
